title: Orion Tech — POC timeline & milestones
next_steps: Maya to send POC proposal & SOW by 2025-11-22
Leo to share benchmark plan + test harness by 2025-11-25
Samir to provide sample dataset, concurrency targets, and infra diagram by 2025-11-24
action_items: Maya Chen: prepare SOW + pricing options (hosted vs dedicated) — due 2025-11-22
Leo Park: design benchmark plan (latency/cost/throughput) and test scripts — due 2025-11-25
Samir Desai (Orion): share 1 week sample of request traces, seq length distribution, and SSO details — due 2025-11-24
summary: POC scoping focused on timeline and milestones for a 6-week pilot to validate latency and cost targets. Agreement on kickoff, access/setup, midpoint benchmark, and exec readout. Security requirements (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS) and dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs discussed. Next steps: SOW, benchmark plan, data access, and schedule kickoff.
topics: Success criteria: p99 latency < 250ms for 512 tokens, accuracy/regression thresholds
Workload sizing: concurrency 50-100 rps, average seq len 200 tokens, peak bursts 200 rps
Benchmarks: latency, throughput, cost-per-token, quality regression checks using golden prompts
Timeline & milestones: kickoff, access/setup, mid-point review, exec readout
transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the account, with Leo Park from SE. Jordan, Riya, Samir, thanks for making time.
[00:18] Jordan Alvarez: Yeah thanks Maya. We wanna get clarity on the POC timeline and what success looks like — we are on a tight Q1 roll out so timing matters.
[00:30] Leo Park: Totally, quick agenda: align on success criteria, workload sizing, bench plan, and then milestone dates — kickoff, access, mid point, exec readout. Does that work?
[00:45] Riya Patel: Yep, that's good. Also we need to make sure security and SSO are covered up front — can't have data flowing until SAML and KMS are validated.

[01:02] Maya Chen: Agreed. High level POC proposal is 6 weeks: 1 week kickoff & access, 3 weeks ramp + benchmarks, 1 week mid-point review, 1 week exec readout and wrap. We can shorten/lengthen depending on scope.
[01:30] Samir Desai: Can you confirm what environment? Hosted API vs Dedicated? We have strict PII rules so likely dedicated or private VPC is preferred.

[01:45] Leo Park: Understood — for the POC we usually run in a dedicated tenant with customer VPC peering when needed. For Orion, if you need on-prem we can discuss private deployment but that extends timeline. For dedicated, we can get you isolated pools and KMS integ.
[02:10] Jordan Alvarez: Timeline hit if we need private on-prem packaging. Let's aim to validate in a dedicated cloud setup with KMS + SSO so we don't get blocked.
[02:25] Maya Chen: Sounds sensible. Success criteria — what matters most? Performance, cost, and output quality. Do you have target numbers?

[02:40] Riya Patel: From platform side: p99 latency under 250ms for our typical requests (we're 512 token-ish), sustained concurrency of 50-100 requests/sec, and peak bursts to 200. Cost target is less strict in POC but we'd like visibility into per-token economics.

[03:05] Samir Desai: From ML side, we need regression checks — baseline against current finetuned model: top-1 accuracy, hallucination rate under 3% on our test set. We'll provide golden prompts and eval script.

[03:30] Leo Park: Good — so benchmarks will measure latency (p50/p90/p99), throughput (rps), and quality metrics via your eval harness. We'll run both streaming and non-streaming, and test model variants and quantization profiles to hit cost/latency targets.
[03:55] Jordan Alvarez: How long to get access? We need the test keys, VPC peering details and sample infra. Also security questionnaire.

[04:10] Maya Chen: We can get an initial test key and staging workspace within 3 business days after the SOW. VPC peering typically 5-7 days depending on your network team. I'll send the security package (SOC2, ISO, data flow diagram) with the SOW.
[04:30] Riya Patel: For SAML SSO, we use Okta — what's Redwood's SAML maturity?

[04:40] Leo Park: We support SAML/Okta for console access and role-based tokens for API. For POC you can use scoped API keys while SAML is being validated; for the exec readout we'll demonstrate full SAML integration in staging.

[04:58] Samir Desai: Ok. On workload sizing — we'll share a week of request traces. Average seq len around 200 tokens, about 1k requests/day currently but that's low; expected production concurrency is higher so POC should simulate 50-100 rps sustained with short bursts.
[05:18] Leo Park: Please include distribution of sequence lengths and any long-tail heavy prompts — that affects KV cache and kernel selection. We'll model batching accordingly.
[05:35] Jordan Alvarez: What about cost experiments? We want both baseline with our current hosted provider and Redwood dedicated numbers.

[05:45] Maya Chen: We'll provide cost modeling: per-token cost, cost per 1M tokens, and cost to run your workload under different models (fp16 vs int8/quant). We'll also show batching tradeoffs and autoscale effects.
[06:00] Riya Patel: For benchmarks, can you run both open model and Redwood-verified variants? Our compliance team won't allow blackbox outputs w/o logging. We need audit logs.
[06:15] Leo Park: Audit logs and request/response logging are available in Dedicated with retention options. We'll document where logs live and how KMS keys are used to encrypt at rest.
[06:30] Samir Desai: Good. About the mid-point review — what do you typically show?

[06:40] Maya Chen: Midpoint is a working demo with benchmark results, identified regressions, and recommended optimizations (e.g., quantization profile, batch sizes). Also an infra checklist: SAML, VPC, KMS status.
[06:55] Jordan Alvarez: Exec readout — we want an ROI slide and recommended next steps (production architecture + cost estimate). Can you do that?

[07:05] Leo Park: Yes — we'll prepare an exec deck with: 1) summary metrics vs targets, 2) performance/cost tradeoffs, 3) recommended configuration for production + estimated monthly costs, and 4) risks and mitigations.
[07:20] Riya Patel: Who owns the benchmark scripts? We prefer to run in our infra to validate latency realistically.

[07:30] Leo Park: We can run both — Redwood-run benchmarks in our dedicated staging, and we can give you the harness to run inside your environment. That will give you direct p99 numbers behind your networking.
[07:45] Samir Desai: We'll run the harness too. Important that the harness includes cold start tests, warm cache, and KV-cache behavior for long conversations.
[07:58] Leo Park: We'll include cold/warm scenarios and explicit KV cache measurements. Also will test autofs scaling and graceful fallback to smaller model variants if capacity constrained.
[08:15] Jordan Alvarez: Any blockers from security? We need KMS integration and to confirm key rotation policies.
[08:25] Maya Chen: We'll include key rotation docs and KMS integration notes. If there's a need for HSM we can discuss; that usually adds lead time but it's doable.

[08:40] Riya Patel: Ok. For acceptance criteria, propose: 1) p99 < 250ms for 512 tokens, 2) cost per 1M tokens below $X (TBD), 3) quality regression < 2-3% on your golden set. If met, proceed to pilot procurement.
[09:05] Maya Chen: That sounds like a solid set. We'll align on the cost target once we see your trace and expected monthly volume. We'll add a grace corridor for early optimization.
[09:20] Samir Desai: On data: we'll mask PII in the sample set, but want to ensure log retention and deletion policies are explicit.
[09:30] Leo Park: We'll send the data handling and retention policy. You can request specific retention windows; logs can be configured to auto-delete after X days.
[09:45] Jordan Alvarez: How about SLA and uptime expectations during POC? We need to ensure availability for the benchmark runs.

[09:55] Maya Chen: POC is operated in a production-like environment; we'll commit to a reasonable uptime window for the dedicated pool and provide runbooks. Enterprise SLA will be discussed for production contracts.
[10:10] Riya Patel: Let's tentatively schedule kickoff Dec 1st. That gives us time to sign SOW and hand off to our infra team for peering.

[10:22] Maya Chen: Sounds good — I will send SOW by Nov 22 and propose Dec 1 kickoff. Key milestones: kickoff (12/1), access & peering done (12/8), benchmarking window (12/9-12/29), mid-point review (12/20), exec readout (12/30). We can compress if needed.
[10:45] Samir Desai: Mid-point on 12/20 works — that lets us have 2 full weeks of benchmarks before the review.

[10:55] Leo Park: For the benchmark plan: we'll run baseline model, two quantization profiles (int8 and fp16), and a fallback smaller variant. We'll measure per-token cost and p99 latency across those.
[11:10] Riya Patel: Please include step-by-step checklist for our network team (CIDR ranges, contact). We can't start peering blind.
[11:22] Maya Chen: I'll include a network checklist and point of contact. Also will attach the security pack and SOC2 report.
[11:35] Jordan Alvarez: Any legal procurement triggers? We may need a DPA and standard MSAs for production — not a blocker for POC but flagging it.
[11:45] Maya Chen: Noted — I'll surface procurement docs. For the POC we can use a short form SOW and attach a DPA as needed.
[11:58] Samir Desai: Small note — our internal benchmarking is sensitive to jitter. Can you also measure tail latencies under noisy neighbors?
[12:08] Leo Park: We'll include noise testing and also show how autoscaling reacts to burst. We'll capture p50/p90/p99 and CPU/GPU utilization charts.
[12:25] Riya Patel: Great. If all good, next steps are SOW, sample data, and schedule kickoff. Any other asks?
[12:35] Maya Chen: Nothing else from our side. Recap of next steps: SOW by 11/22, benchmark plan by 11/25, sample data by 11/24, kickoff 12/1. We'll confirm calendar invites.
[12:50] Jordan Alvarez: Thanks team — we'll aim to get the artifacts over this week.
[13:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up over email and attach the docs. Talk soon.
[13:08] (call ends)
